# Customitin: start here for coding agents

Customitin is a local-first React Native personalization SDK. This repository is a functional alpha. Packages are local/unpublished; use workspaces or built tarballs. Do not recommend an npm registry installation until a release actually exists.

This documentation describes implemented contracts. It is intended to let a developer's coding agent integrate the SDK without handing a developer a registry to fill in manually. Read the consuming app's instructions first, inspect its existing code, and reuse its data clients, authentication and components.

## Reading order

1. [Integration playbook](integration.md): shortest path from an existing app to a working integration.
2. [Contracts and examples](contracts.md): source loaders, query factories, pagination, components and routes.
3. [Overrides and maintenance](maintenance.md): ownership, persistent identities, refresh and removal.
4. [Troubleshooting and verification](troubleshooting.md): actionable diagnostics and evidence required before claiming success.
5. [CLI reference](cli-reference.md): commands, flags and machine-readable outputs.

In a built CLI package, `customitin guide` prints this page; `customitin guide --topic integration` prints a chapter. `customitin schema` prints the actual JSON Schema for overrides. From this repository use `npm run cli --` before the command instead of `customitin`.

## Product model

A capability registry describes approved components, sources, navigation destinations, theme tokens and customizable surfaces. A source adapter executes a validated query through host code. A saved profile contains configuration, not domain records. A planner proposes schema-validated operations. The mobile runtime previews them and persists only after the user applies them.

To personalize existing UI, use `inspect` and enable supported screen selectors with `init --screen <selector>`. The CLI instruments the selected screen's existing JSX, registers its sections, and mounts a provider around the original app. Each selected screen gets its own customization controls; this mode does not add My space or replace navigation. Users can reorder/hide optional sections, preview/apply, undo, restore the layout, and change connected text sizes/spacing without a planner. Hooks, callbacks and data stay in host code. See [screen contracts](contracts.md#existing-screens).

Without screen selections, generated integrations retain the separate My space/Customize shell. Neither mode migrates every existing screen or style. The CLI keeps visible outer JSX provider chains (names ending in Provider, including Context.Provider) above personalization. Providers hidden inside another component or navigator still need a shared host wrapper. Edit host screens/root normally and use watch --apply alongside the dev server to regenerate section bindings; refresh/remove preserve current host edits. Keep the generated SDK wrapper props/imports intact. See [maintenance](maintenance.md).

## Working rules for integration agents

- Run inspect and use exact reported selectors. Do not invent a source, field, route or provider export.
- Treat discovery as evidence of structure. A return type does not establish completeness, authorization or business meaning.
- Prefer CLI flags or overrides over handwritten capabilities. Use config.ts only for host runtime connections/custom bindings.
- Review exposed fields. Use a fields allowlist when a source contains internal scalar properties.
- Never mark a cached page complete to make filtering work. Never implement remote filtering after pagination.
- Keep model keys on the developer's backend. Runtime auth headers come from the existing app session. Installer AI is optional and separate from runtime AI.
- Keep new UI copy in the SDK English dictionary. Do not generate translations for every language.
- Report exactly which commands passed, which devices were exercised, and which setup remains. Browser tests are not native-device validation.

## Useful implementation entry points (repository relative)

- packages/cli/src/discovery: bounded, static TypeScript inspection; no application execution.
- packages/cli/src/configuration: override schema, stable identities and selection rules.
- packages/cli/src/generation: checked templates for manifests and bindings.
- packages/cli/src/commands: planning, transactional writes, diagnostics and removal.
- packages/react-native/src/adapters/query.ts: cache/remote adapter helpers; no TanStack dependency.
- packages/react-native/src/composer/host.tsx: generated integration's shell.
- packages/core/src/validation: authoritative runtime restrictions.
- tests/installer-discovery.test.ts: compiling consumer examples for supported integrations.
- tests/installer-overrides.test.ts: persistence and refresh contracts.

## Known boundaries

Hook execution remains inside React. Existing-screen instrumentation supports static sections in a vertical View/ScrollView. Conditional roots, virtualized/horizontal layouts, native/custom canvases, required-control semantics, deep custom-component styling, relative-date semantics, theme-system migration and authorization are not automatically inferred. Existing forms can remain inside a section; the SDK preserves their mounted state but does not edit their behavior. Query-option generation currently supports zero-argument factories returning array queries. Infinite queries and factories requiring runtime arguments need a host adapter. React Navigation generation uses explicit ParamList type aliases and an existing exported navigation ref; it does not create a second NavigationContainer.

# Integration playbook for coding agents

## 1. Inspect before generating

Work in the consuming application's workspace, not the whole monorepo. The tested alpha baseline is Node 24.15 (minimum 22.13), React 19.2, React Native 0.83.10, TypeScript 5.9.3, Expo 55.0.31 / Expo Router 55.0.18 when applicable, React Navigation 7.5 / native-stack 7.20, AsyncStorage 2.2, and TanStack Query 5.90.12. The CLI does not upgrade the host framework. Query, navigation and storage integrations are optional and reuse the libraries the app already has.

Packages are unpublished. In a Customitin checkout, run:

```sh
npm ci
npm run pack:local -- /tmp/customitin-packages
```

This builds all four packages, includes the AI guides, writes a packages.json map and prints two exact install commands. Run those printed commands inside the consuming app. The first installs core and react-native together as runtime dependencies. The second installs cli and server together as development dependencies; server is a dependency of the development CLI and must also resolve locally until publication. Do not install only the CLI tarball and let npm search for the unpublished server package. No model credentials are needed for these steps. A backend that uses the planner handler installs its own core/server pair separately.

Once installed, all commands run from the consuming app, with no dependency on the SDK checkout:

```sh
npx --no-install customitin guide --topic integration
npx --no-install customitin inspect
npx --no-install customitin init --dry-run
```

`--no-install` avoids accidentally fetching a similarly named public package. You can also use the local `node_modules/.bin/customitin` executable. Add `--cwd /absolute/path/to/app` when running outside the app. Inside the SDK checkout, `npm run cli -- <command>` remains available for contributors.

For a genuinely new bare app, the official template command for this baseline is:

```sh
npx @react-native-community/cli@20.2.0 init MyApp --version 0.83.10
```

Finish the template's own platform setup before native testing. Install persistent storage if the app has none (`npm install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage@2.2.0`), then run Customitin init so it is detected automatically. Follow the native library's pod/rebuild steps; the CLI does not install or upgrade native libraries. Without persistent storage, init creates an in-memory preview setup and doctor reports the remaining storage work.

`inspect` reports exact selectors such as `src/data.ts#loadEntries`, field rules, component props, query clients, routes, root candidates and unresolved hooks. It does not import or run the host app. Its `context` is hidden unless `--context` is supplied; ordinary inspection uses no external AI.

Use the developer's existing AI to read this report and the application's own repository. Optional `--ai` sends a separately reviewed bounded metadata context to a provider, but is not required to automate integration.

## 2. Make the few semantic decisions once

For existing-screen customization, start with the screen metadata in `inspect`. Enable the intended exported screens (selectors are examples; use the report's actual values):

```sh
npx --no-install customitin init --screen 'src/screens/Home.tsx#Home' --dry-run
npx --no-install customitin init --screen 'src/screens/Home.tsx#Home' --apply
```

Repeat `--screen` for additional screens. No source adapters, navigation ref, hand-written registry, or model key are needed just to personalize an existing screen. The original screen continues to obtain its own data and run its own callbacks. Generated root wiring uses CustomizationProvider, leaving the host navigator in place. The selected screens receive inline controls instead of a separate My space.

After installation, edit the screens' ordinary JSX, hooks and handlers in place. Content/style changes use normal Fast Refresh. Run `npx --no-install customitin watch --apply` alongside the existing dev server to update section registration automatically after structural edits. No removal/reinstall cycle is needed. One-shot `refresh --apply` is also available; keep React section keys stable and leave the generated wrapper ID/sectionIds props alone. See [editable host ownership](maintenance.md#file-ownership).

Supported screens return a vertical React Native View/ScrollView with static JSX sections. Give repeated siblings stable string `key` or `testID` values; wrap mapped/conditional groups in a keyed View. Inspect reports the sections or an actionable reason automatic instrumentation is unavailable. Review the dry-run and mark business-critical sections with `screens[selector].requiredSections` in overrides before shipping. Section labels default to the key/testID or component name. See [exact screen contracts](contracts.md#existing-screens) for layout and appearance boundaries.

A source with @customitinComplete is automatically eligible. For an unannotated array loader you have verified returns the entire authorized collection, use `--complete`. Enable suitable display components and routes using repeatable flags:

```sh
npx --no-install customitin init \
  --complete 'src/data.ts#loadEntries' \
  --component 'src/EntryCard.tsx#EntryCard' \
  --detail 'src/data.ts#loadEntries=src/app/entries/[id].tsx' \
  --dry-run
```

These flags merge into `personalize/overrides.json` when applied. They do not modify the source annotations. Review the exact generated output and developerOwnedSetup, then repeat with `--apply` instead of `--dry-run`.

If several sources match a card's object prop, set the component override's `source` to the intended source selector. For detail navigation set source `detailDestination` to the enabled route selector. A route with exactly one parameter needs no `detailParam`; otherwise automatic detail binding is unavailable. ID and route parameter scalar types must match.

Use `fields` to limit data exposure, `titleField`/`subtitleField` for display, and defaults for required fixed item-card props. The full schema is available through `customitin schema`. Unknown keys and unresolved selectors fail before writes.

## 3. Connect host runtime state

The CLI creates config.ts once. When AsyncStorage is already installed it uses that implementation automatically. Otherwise it starts with memory storage, which doctor reports as a setup issue. Do not ship memory storage if settings must survive a restart.

The generated root calls `useHostConfiguration` when exported. This is the supported place to read the existing session hook and provide reactive scope/session/bindings. For example, adapt this sketch to actual exports in the host:

```tsx
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
import { asyncStorageAdapter } from '@customitin/react-native/storage';
import { createHttpPlanner } from '@customitin/react-native/adapters';
import { useSession, getSessionHeaders } from '../auth';

export const storage = asyncStorageAdapter(AsyncStorage);
export const scope = 'signed-out';
export const planner = createHttpPlanner({
  url: 'https://your-backend.example/plan',
  getHeaders: getSessionHeaders,
});

export function useHostConfiguration() {
  const session = useSession();
  const bindings = useMemo(() => ({ session }), [session]);
  return { scope: session?.localProfileKey ?? 'signed-out', bindings };
}
```

`localProfileKey` above is illustrative, not an SDK session property. Choose the app's actual stable opaque account scope. Change it immediately on logout/account switching. The SDK clears active personalization and cancels pending work when its scope changes. Host query keys/authentication must also isolate users.

The generated root merges custom sources, components and items over generated bindings. `bindings.navigate` can replace generated navigation. Custom hooks must be under their required providers. The CLI preserves visible outer JSX provider chains whose names end in Provider (including Context.Provider). Providers hidden inside other components or navigators need a shared host wrapper arranged before init. Edit an installed host root normally while retaining its PersonalizationRoot boundary; refresh preserves the changes and recalculates supported provider placement. Do not hand-edit personalize/root.tsx. Keep options and custom bindings stable/memoized to avoid unnecessary runtime resets or data reloads.

## 4. Connect the assistant

Manual appearance and saved layouts work without a planner. The generated scaffold does not pretend to understand arbitrary prompts offline. For natural language, deploy a developer-owned authenticated endpoint with the generated server-manifest.json.

The backend uses createPlannerHandler from @customitin/server. Supply manifests, a verified-session authenticate callback, an allowRequest quota callback, and an OpenAI/Anthropic/custom provider. Validate environment configuration at startup. Keep provider keys on the server; getHeaders on mobile sends the existing user's session, not the provider key.

The backend must serve the registry revision used by the mobile build. Retain supported older manifests during rollout. The planner is stateless and does not require a profile database. The repository's loopback demo server is for local demonstrations, not a deployment template with production authentication already completed.

## 5. Verify and hand off

```sh
npx --no-install customitin doctor --typecheck
```

Then run the host's lint, tests and bundle commands. Doctor's typecheck is static; it never runs arbitrary package scripts. Exercise Original app, Customize, preview, apply, My space, saved views, detail navigation, undo, reset, restart and account switching. For query-backed collections, mutate data through the original workflow and verify the personal view refreshes.

Report the actual connected source/component/route names, storage, account scope, planner status, checks and manual deployment/device work. Commit generated files, overrides, config and bindings.lock.json together. Subsequent app changes use refresh, not a new manually written registry.

For selected existing screens, exercise each original route, customize its layout, hide/show a section containing local state, apply, restart, undo, and restore. Confirm the app's existing callbacks and provider context still work. Check native layout, keyboard/focus and accessibility because section wrappers can affect flex geometry. Text scaling applies only to explicit fontSize/lineHeight values in connected Text nodes, and compact spacing scales numeric gap/rowGap/columnGap values. It does not restyle imported custom component internals.

When no screens are selected, the generated My space initially displays a welcome message. Registering sources, cards and routes makes them available for proposals; it does not automatically insert them into a saved layout. Appearance controls work immediately without a planner. See [testing](testing.md) for a deterministic proposal that exercises data/card/navigation integration without buying model credits, and for the native Jest setup. Do not ship the test planner as a natural-language assistant.

When react-native-safe-area-context is already installed, generation connects its provider/insets to the SDK shell automatically. Personal panels and shell buttons stay inside the safe area while the original navigator retains its own layout. The SDK itself has no mandatory safe-area dependency; custom hosts can pass insets directly to PersonalizationHost.

# Supported contracts and adapter examples

Examples use fictional host exports. They are patterns to map to the consuming app, not instructions to replace working business logic.

## Complete repositories

Discovery supports exported function declarations, exported arrow/function expressions and callable methods on exported repository objects. Methods are invoked on the imported object so their `this` receiver is retained. Complete automatic array loaders take no parameters and return typed mutable/readonly arrays or promises of arrays.

```ts
interface Entry {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  stage: 'draft' | 'done';
  note?: string;
}

/** @customitinComplete */
export const loadEntries = async (): Promise<Entry[]> => repository.readAll();
```

The marker asserts all authorized rows are returned within the declared row budget. It is not justified by an array return type, a successful fetch, or a cache containing several pages. Without it, use a reviewed source override with completeness: "complete". Other exported sources remain unchanged.

Strings, numbers, booleans, literal enums and nullable/optional scalar fields are discovered. Nested objects and executable fields are not exposed. Optional row values normalize to null. The ID field must be a non-nullable string or number; override idField for `_id`, `uuid`, etc. Every returned row is validated and duplicate IDs are rejected. The adapter projects only the registry's exposed fields before validation/rendering.

## TanStack Query

```ts
import { QueryClient, queryOptions } from '@tanstack/react-query';
export const queryClient = new QueryClient(); // Reuse the app's actual existing instance.

/** @customitinComplete */
export const entryOptions = () =>
  queryOptions({
    queryKey: ['entries'],
    queryFn: loadEntries,
  });
```

Export an existing QueryClient rather than introducing a second one. When exactly one client is discovered, generation binds it automatically; otherwise select `queryClient` in overrides or use --query-client. The generated adapter calls fetchQuery, keeps the original options, appends `customitin-scope` and the active local scope to the query key, and sets staleTime to zero for refreshes. It uses the same client but a scoped cache entry; it does not claim to share the original exact cache key.

Invalidation of the host key prefix (for example `['entries']`) refreshes personal collections. Manual cache writes on matching keys also notify them. Ordinary fetch-success events do not trigger a new fetch, preventing feedback loops. Exact-key invalidation of only the original key may leave scoped entries unaffected at the cache level, but the bridge observes the matching invalidation event and refreshes the personal source.

Cancellation stops the personalized request from accepting a late result. A shared host fetch is not forcibly cancelled by the bridge; its own query function/client controls network cancellation. Existing session checks and account-scoped host data remain the application's responsibility.

Supported factories currently take no parameters and return query options whose query function returns a typed array. Infinite queries, hooks, unexported clients and factories requiring account/filter arguments need a custom config binding or a small exported host wrapper. Discovery does not invoke hooks or flatten arbitrary useInfiniteQuery caches.

## Paginated queries

Use an explicit remote query contract when the host already supports typed filter/sort operations and cursors:

```ts
import type { QueryContext, ValidatedQuery } from '@customitin/core';

/** @customitinQuery */
export async function queryEntries(
  query: ValidatedQuery,
  context: QueryContext,
  cursor?: string,
): Promise<{
  items: Entry[];
  nextCursor: string | null;
  complete: boolean;
  totalCount?: number;
}> {
  return existingClient.queryEntries(
    query,
    context.session,
    cursor,
    context.signal,
  );
}
```

The argument order above is the contract. The host verifies authorization and applies mandatory tenant restrictions independently of user filters. Filter and sort happen before cursor pagination. totalCount, if supplied, is the matching total, not the number loaded. Return complete: true only with nextCursor: null.

Remote filter/sort capabilities default to empty. Declare supported operators explicitly:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "sources": {
    "src/data.ts#queryEntries": {
      "filters": { "stage": ["eq"], "title": ["contains"] },
      "sortable": ["title"],
      "pageSize": 30,
      "maxRows": 500
    }
  }
}
```

A string field does not prove a remote server supports contains. Grouping over paginated/partial sources is unavailable. A backend with another pagination protocol needs a small wrapper implementing the contract; the CLI does not guess URL parameters or SQL.

## Components

Use --component, enabled: true, or @customitinComponent to opt a discovered component into generation. Function components with scalar props become host sections; components with one scalar-record object prop can become item renderers when exactly one compatible source is selected. Optional onPress callbacks connect to registered detail navigation. Other required callbacks, React children, complex object props and context requirements need a host wrapper.

```tsx
export function EntryCard({
  entry,
  onPress,
}: {
  entry: Entry;
  onPress?: () => void;
}) {
  return (
    <Pressable onPress={onPress}>
      <Text>{entry.title}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

The generator matches actual field types/nullability/enums. If several sources fit, use the component's source selector. Item renderers get a sourceIds restriction enforced by core validation; the planner cannot reuse a bound renderer with an unrelated source. Required extra item props need defaults. Host scalar props remain configurable; supplied defaults fill omitted values. Components are registered for possible layouts; they are not automatically inserted into the original screen.

## Navigation

Expo Router discovery reads app/ or src/app/ TSX routes, skips layouts and special + files, and extracts single dynamic parameters. Catch-all/array routes need custom navigation. Enabling a route generates a createNavigationAdapter closure using the existing router; discovery alone does not enable it.

React Navigation discovery reads explicit TypeScript type aliases ending in ParamList. Export the existing createNavigationContainerRef result and ensure it is attached to the host container. With one discovered ref it is selected automatically; otherwise use navigationRef/--navigation-ref. Generated closures check isReady and call the existing ref with typed screen names/params. Nested NavigatorScreenParams and arbitrary navigation hooks require host code.

For details, source detailDestination references an enabled route selector or stable ID. Automatic row-to-route mapping supports exactly one parameter of the same scalar type as the ID. Multi-parameter destinations remain available as shortcuts but need a custom detail binding.

## Existing screens

`--screen <file#export>` opts a discovered function/arrow component into in-place customization, including a default-export App. The component can keep props, hooks, closures, session context and existing callbacks: its JSX remains in the original lexical scope. This is separate from `--component`, which registers reusable content for composed surfaces.

Supported automatic structure:

```tsx
export function Home() {
  const account = useAccount();
  return (
    <ScrollView contentContainerStyle={{ gap: 16 }}>
      <AccountHeader key="account" account={account} />
      <View key="recommendations">
        {account.showRecommendations && <Recommendations />}
      </View>
      <CheckoutButton key="checkout" onPress={account.checkout} />
    </ScrollView>
  );
}
```

The CLI derives a `kind: "screen"` surface and a stable node for each section. Identity comes from a static string key, then a static testID, then a unique JSX tag. Repeated identities are rejected rather than assigned array-index identities. Do not change these identities to repurpose saved sections. Mark non-hideable controls in developer-owned overrides:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "screens": {
    "src/screens/Home.tsx#Home": {
      "enabled": true,
      "requiredSections": ["checkout"]
    }
  }
}
```

The SDK cannot infer business-critical controls; unmarked sections can be hidden. Required sections can move but cannot be omitted or changed. Core validation permits only exact existing nodes, reordered or with optional nodes omitted. It rejects new section identities, duplicate sections, changed props, and injected components. Screen-specific planner requests carry `surfaceId`; both client and server reject changes to other layouts or navigation. Declared theme preferences remain shared across connected screens.

Generated JSX uses `CustomizableLayout` with a screen ID, generated sectionIds map and one ordinary JSX container child. Developers edit the container's keyed JSX children, hooks, callbacks and styles directly. The CLI adds stable React keys to initially unkeyed sections. CustomizableLayout maps those keys to registered nodes and delegates to the lower-level CustomizableScreen (sections map plus render-function child). It clones the container to supply ordered content while retaining its original type, props and ref. Each section gets a stable native View wrapper. Hidden sections stay mounted with display:none and accessibility exclusion, preserving local state and host subscriptions. Hiding is presentation only, not authorization or suspension of background work. The editor is rendered inside the original container; use a scrollable host when content/controls can exceed the viewport.

Content/style edits work immediately. Add/remove/default-order changes need refresh or watch --apply to regenerate the registry; identities of unchanged keyed sections survive. While JSX keys and registry nodes differ, CustomizableLayout renders the current host container with customization temporarily unavailable. Structural saves during development can remount sections. This fallback does not synchronize a production server manifest; refresh and deploy matching manifests before releasing the app. See [maintenance](maintenance.md).

Directly referenced React Native Text/View/ScrollView primitives inside the selected JSX are connected to ScreenText/ScreenView/ScreenScrollView. Props, refs and styles are forwarded. Explicit fontSize/lineHeight numbers scale with type.scale; numeric gap/rowGap/columnGap values scale to 65% for compact density. Until a user chooses a preference, original values remain. Colors, images, padding, absolute positioning, custom fonts and opaque component internals are not inferred or restyled. These require a host theme bridge or custom integration. The inline generator therefore declares text-scale and density tokens, not the SDK light/dark palettes.

Limits: 1–40 static direct JSX sections, a single unconditional return, and a directly imported vertical View/ScrollView container. Wrap conditional/mapped contents in a stable section. Conditional root returns, FlatList/SectionList roots, horizontal/custom containers, stickyHeaderIndices, maintainVisibleContentPosition and ambiguous sections need a host integration. Added section wrappers may change flex-dependent layouts, sticky-header indexing, clipping or native focus behavior; validate actual device geometry before release. Screens with such container contracts should use a reviewed custom integration. Shared visible provider chains remain above the SDK provider; hidden providers still need host review.

Screen selection adds no data loaders and exposes no JSX bodies, records or callbacks to the model. Natural language still needs a configured planner. Manual layout and appearance controls work offline. Persistence and account isolation follow the existing storage/scope contracts.

# Overrides, identities and maintenance

## File ownership

| File                               | Owner                       | Behavior                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| personalize/config.ts              | Developer                   | Created once; never overwritten or removed by refresh/remove                        |
| personalize/overrides.json         | Developer                   | Created once; CLI selection flags explicitly merge requested decisions              |
| personalize/bindings.lock.json     | Installer                   | Stable IDs and previous selectors; retained on removal; commit this file            |
| personalize/capabilities.json      | Installer                   | Mobile registry generated from discovery plus overrides                             |
| personalize/server-manifest.json   | Installer                   | Matching backend registry; deploy with planner                                      |
| personalize/sources.ts             | Installer                   | Data adapter bindings                                                               |
| personalize/components.tsx         | Installer                   | Host/item wrappers                                                                  |
| personalize/navigation.ts          | Installer                   | Approved destination closures                                                       |
| personalize/root.tsx               | Installer                   | Provider/shell integration and custom binding merge                                 |
| .customitin/ownership.json         | Installer                   | Generated hashes, reversible host bindings and unwrapped host snapshots             |
| Root and selected screen TSX files | Developer with SDK wrappers | Host code stays editable; only recognized SDK imports/props/wrappers are maintained |

Do not edit installer-owned files to customize behavior. Change overrides or supply runtime bindings through config.ts, then refresh. Existing generated-file edits block replacement/removal rather than being silently discarded. Developer config, overrides and the identity lock remain on removal. Retaining the lock keeps moved/renamed selector overrides usable if the integration is installed again.

Edit selected screens and the app root normally: JSX content, props, styles, hooks, callbacks, imports and surrounding providers belong to the developer. Generated screens keep ordinary nested JSX inside CustomizableLayout. The CLI supplies a static sectionIds map and adds stable React keys where missing. Keep section keys stable; an added key remains ordinary host code if an edited screen is later removed from the integration.

Discovery and refresh unwrap recognized SDK syntax from the **current** file, retain host edits and regenerate the bindings. Formatting changes are accepted. Removing the integration or disabling a screen strips only SDK instrumentation from the latest source; an unchanged host file is restored byte-for-byte from its unwrapped snapshot. Root edits are preserved too. Removing a section, adding a section, or changing its default order requires regeneration, while content/style/handler changes work immediately through normal Fast Refresh.

Do not hand-edit generated wrapper imports, aliases, IDs or sectionIds. Changes to those boundaries stop refresh/removal with diagnostics and no writes. Restore the indicated SDK syntax; there is no need to remove/reinstall the integration. Ordinary generated adapters under personalize/ retain whole-file drift protection. Never edit ownership hashes to bypass checks. Older installations without reversible host metadata upgrade on a refresh when their tracked host files are unchanged; if already modified, preserve those edits and restore the last generated host version before upgrading, then reapply the edits.

A moved screen is recognized only when its original path is absent and exactly one new file retains its complete SDK wrapper. A unique unchanged export name keeps the existing identity; use an explicit symbol override for renames. Ambiguous copies, splitting/merging instrumented files and modified wrapper aliases need deliberate host wiring or restoring the known SDK boundaries first. No move is inferred from a partial match.

## Complete override example

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "sources": {
    "src/data.ts#loadEntries": {
      "enabled": true,
      "completeness": "complete",
      "title": "Entries",
      "fields": ["id", "title", "stage"],
      "idField": "id",
      "titleField": "title",
      "maxRows": 500,
      "detailDestination": "src/app/entries/[id].tsx"
    }
  },
  "components": {
    "src/EntryCard.tsx#EntryCard": {
      "enabled": true,
      "source": "src/data.ts#loadEntries",
      "defaults": {}
    }
  },
  "routes": {
    "src/app/entries/[id].tsx": { "enabled": true, "title": "Entry details" }
  }
}
```

Only use actual discovered selectors. The example is not universally applicable: if EntryCard requires an excluded field such as note, include it or adapt the host card. Defaults must satisfy the component's scalar rules. Use the JSON Schema produced by `customitin schema` as the authoritative list of supported properties.

`enabled: false` disables a discovered capability without changing application code. Disabling a source can make dependent card bindings unavailable; diagnostics report the mismatch. A field allowlist controls what gets projected to SDK collections. It does not change the host repository.

## Stable identity

The lock records a persistent ID, current selector and previous selectors for each discovered capability. On refresh, an exact selector keeps its ID. A unique export name of the same kind moved to another file can also keep its ID. Ambiguous names do not get guessed. Previous selectors remain aliases, so existing override keys still resolve after a file move.

For a rename or an ambiguous move, retain the old override key or stable ID and point `symbol` to the new selector:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "sources": {
    "src/data.ts#loadEntries": {
      "symbol": "src/repository.ts#readEntries",
      "title": "Entries"
    }
  }
}
```

Use this only for the same logical capability. Rebinding a source ID to unrelated data can make saved filters misleading. The CLI preserves identity, not business equivalence.

Manifest revisions are derived from capability semantics, excluding evidence file/line locations. Moving an otherwise unchanged source does not obsolete profiles. Changing fields, operators, labels or binding restrictions can change the revision. Deploy the new server manifest and retain older supported revisions. When a field disappears, runtime reconciliation disables incompatible views rather than removing restrictive filters.

Bindings missing from the current scan remain in the lock as identity history. Overrides that refer to missing active bindings produce diagnostics. Update symbol or explicitly disable them. The lock also stores optional installer-AI source selections, so a later refresh without --ai retains the choice.

Pre-lock installations import matching original source IDs when possible. If a legacy source moved or was renamed before the first upgrade refresh, review the old manifest and restore its selector first or perform an explicit reviewed migration. Do not delete the lock to resolve conflicts.

## Refresh workflow

For normal development, run this alongside the app's existing Metro/Expo/dev command, or add it as a parallel process to an existing development script:

```sh
npx --no-install customitin watch --apply
```

Watch requires an installed integration. It polls bounded source files, overrides, config and tracked output once per second, serializes regeneration and reports changed files or actionable issues as JSON lines. It never runs host scripts or invokes installer AI. Without --apply it only reports plans; --dry-run takes precedence. Stop with Ctrl+C. Edits arriving during planning cause that plan to be skipped and retried on a later poll. Unsupported JSX or altered SDK boundaries keep the last generated integration intact; save a supported correction and watch resumes. Newly added/removed sections show the host container without customization controls while registration is stale, so a save does not hide new UI or throw a section mismatch error. Structural changes can remount sections during this development transition.

Watch is optional. A one-shot workflow is also supported:

1. Update the host code directly; keep section keys stable.
2. Run inspect; compare actual signatures and fields.
3. Update only overrides/config as needed.
4. Run refresh --dry-run and review changed files, unresolved items and conflicts.
5. Apply the same plan with refresh --apply.
6. Run doctor --typecheck and the host's lint/tests/bundles.
7. Exercise a previously saved profile and any changed data/navigation behavior.
8. Deploy matching backend manifests before requiring them in a new app build.

Before a release, run refresh --apply, doctor --typecheck and the app's checks even if watch was running. Review and commit source/generated changes together, including .customitin/ownership.json and bindings.lock.json. Deploy matching server manifests when capability semantics change. Do not run multiple applying CLI processes against the same app at once.

## What refresh does not do

It does not run application modules, silently change credentials, upgrade frameworks, infer tenant restrictions, merge arbitrary custom code, migrate all existing styles, deploy a backend, or publish a mobile release. These remain explicit host implementation/release tasks.

## Generated formatting

The CLI formats generated TypeScript and the root wrapper before recording ownership hashes. It reads portable literal settings from JSON prettier files, package.json.prettier, and simple module.exports/export-default object configs. It never executes a host configuration or loads formatter plugins. Dynamic configs, YAML, overrides and custom plugins fall back to portable defaults; these are not a promise to reproduce every host formatting rule. To change generated output, adjust a supported static config and refresh before running a formatter over installer-owned files. Check TypeScript files explicitly: the default bare React Native lint script may only scan JavaScript unless `--ext .js,.jsx,.ts,.tsx` is supplied.


---

<!-- Source: docs/ai/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting and verification

## Read the diagnostic, then inspect its evidence

| Symptom                              | Likely cause                                                            | Action                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source listed but not generated      | Completeness is unknown                                                 | Verify the repository, then use --complete or a completeness override               |
| Query factory skipped                | No unique exported QueryClient                                          | Export/select the existing client; do not create a replacement cache                |
| Hook requires adapter                | Discovery found useSomething                                            | Expose an underlying query factory or provide a React-safe host binding             |
| Card has no unique source            | More than one matching row shape, or required fields excluded           | Set component.source or correct the field selection                                 |
| Component requires unsupported props | Callback, children, object or provider dependency cannot be synthesized | Export a small wrapper with a supported interface                                   |
| Remote filters unavailable           | No explicit server operator contract                                    | Declare supported filters/sort fields after verifying endpoint behavior             |
| Detail parameter mismatch            | Row ID and route parameter differ in type/count                         | Use compatible schema or a custom navigation/data binding                           |
| No navigation ref                    | React Navigation ref is absent or ambiguous                             | Export/select the ref already attached to the root navigator                        |
| Root needs manual integration        | HOC, conditional return or unsupported root expression                  | Place PersonalizationRoot in the appropriate existing provider tree                 |
| Settings vanish on restart           | Memory storage                                                          | Install/connect persistent host storage                                             |
| Planner unavailable                  | No endpoint, invalid session, revision mismatch or provider failure     | Verify backend configuration and matching manifest; inspect safe server diagnostics |
| Refresh required                     | Source/override/template changed                                        | Review refresh --dry-run, then apply and recheck                                    |
| Drift                                | Someone edited an owned file                                            | Preserve those edits in config/host code; resolve deliberately before regeneration  |
| SDK wrapper props/imports changed    | A generated host boundary was altered                                   | Restore the indicated SDK syntax; ordinary host JSX/logic can remain edited         |
| Project changed while planning       | A new save arrived during regeneration                                  | Let watch retry after the next save settles, or rerun refresh                       |

Generated sources and routes are typed but still depend on truthful host contracts. A passing typecheck does not prove completeness, correct filtering, authorization or visual quality.

## SDK contributor checks

Run `npm run check` after changes. It includes strict TypeScript, zero-warning lint, formatting, unit/integration tests, package builds and mobile dependency/domain boundaries. Relevant tests include:

- installer-discovery: compile real consumer integrations against installed framework types.
- installer-overrides: field exposure, identity through moves/renames, selection persistence and conflict preservation.
- query-adapters: remote query/cursor forwarding, row projection, cache notifications and cancellation.
- host-ui: preview/apply, saved-view navigation, detail navigation and original-screen state preservation.
- installer: baseline install/idempotency/remove, context exclusion and ownership behavior.

Run `npm run test:e2e` for browser interactions across the recipe/movie/task reference apps. Browser prerequisites include a Playwright Chromium installation. A missing browser, blocked port or native toolchain problem must be reported as a limitation, not as a passing check.

## Consumer checks

Use `doctor --typecheck` to include TypeScript diagnostics from the consuming app's tsconfig and generated integration. This performs static analysis, not host script execution. It reports up to 50 TypeScript diagnostics. Run the app's own lint/tests/bundle scripts separately using its documented workflow.

Verify these behaviors with the developer's actual app:

1. Original app navigation and unsaved screen state survive entering/leaving customization.
2. Manual appearance changes require preview/apply and survive restart with persistent storage.
3. A planner proposal cannot reference unregistered fields/components/routes.
4. Filters match the complete authorized dataset, including records beyond the first page.
5. Paginated results have stable IDs, no duplicate rows and meaningful counts.
6. Existing mutations update personal views through cache invalidation/custom subscriptions.
7. Tapping an item uses the existing detail workflow.
8. Logout/account switching clears active personalization and cannot render late old-user results.
9. Undo/reset and storage failure recovery behave correctly.
10. Existing saved views remain usable after a compatible refresh; incompatible views fail conservatively.

See [testing.md](testing.md) for the packed-consumer regression command, Jest configuration and native bundling commands. Run native iOS/Android builds and device checks before a production release. Check VoiceOver/TalkBack, larger text, keyboard navigation where applicable, safe areas, screen-reader visibility of the hidden original view, scrolling/memory with large collections, and lifecycle behavior while the host screen remains mounted. Generated personal navigation lives inside My space; it is not a rewrite of the host's native tab bar.

## Completion report template

State which sources, components and routes were connected; whether storage is persistent; how scope/auth are connected; whether the planner was exercised with a live provider; and the actual checks executed. List remaining manual deployment, native device or unsupported-pattern work plainly. Do not claim a fully automatic integration when the report still contains unresolved required bindings.


---

<!-- Source: docs/ai/testing.md -->

# Verify a real consuming app

Use the app's actual installed packages, native types and scripts. A workspace test with TypeScript path aliases does not prove that the published artifacts work. Do not hand-edit generated code to get a test passing: fix the SDK or developer-owned host configuration, then refresh.

## Existing-screen acceptance

Run `npm run check` in the SDK checkout. The screen consumer fixtures compile generated named/default/root-screen integrations with strict unused-import checks. Generated-screen interaction tests execute the instrumented app with React Native Web: existing provider context and callbacks, reorder/hide/show, retained form drafts, in-place typography previews, discard/apply, restart restoration, undo and restoring the original layout. Core/server tests reject replacement section IDs, changed props, duplicate/required-node removal and planner changes outside the requested screen. These are deterministic component tests, not native-device or live-model acceptance.

Editable-host fixtures cover JSX/handler/style edits, added/removed sections, stable IDs, formatter changes, a moved screen, removal/disable preserving unrefreshed edits, and refusing changed SDK boundaries or unsupported containers. Watch tests cover applied saves, dry-run without writes and cancellation. A generated-consumer interaction test shows new UI while the registry is stale, then hides/shows the new section after refresh. On devices, also verify the real Metro/Expo Fast Refresh sequence while watch is running; the component test rebuilds bundles and does not claim to emulate the dev server.

For an actual --screen integration, exercise the same actions on iOS and Android. Verify original geometry (especially flex-dependent children), scrolling with the inline editor open, sticky headers, keyboard focus when hiding forms, accessibility exclusion of hidden sections, account switching, storage failures and the original navigation. Hidden sections remain mounted, so subscriptions/effects continue. No physical-device, performance or live-provider claim is implied by the fixture suite. Deploy the new matching manifest and server package before using surfaceId-aware planner requests.

## Reproduce the fresh-app acceptance test

From a Customitin checkout with dependencies installed:

```sh
npm run test:consumer
```

This downloads the official React Native 0.83.10 template into a new temporary directory, builds/packs all SDK packages, installs those tarballs with their actual dependencies, and runs the packaged CLI. It does not use workspace symlinks or source aliases. Network access and a supported Node version are required. Set `npm_config_cache` to a writable directory when working in a sandbox.

The command prints the fresh app and evidence directories and leaves them available for inspection. It checks:

- Unmodified template init, doctor/typecheck, removal and original-root restoration.
- A small independent trail app with a complete TanStack query, shared QueryClientProvider, custom item card, a host component requiring query context, AsyncStorage and React Navigation details.
- Inspect, dry-run without root writes, durable CLI choices, idempotent refresh and a source move.
- Host TypeScript, explicit zero-warning TypeScript lint, native React component interactions and iOS/Android Metro production bundles.
- Preview/apply, full-data filtering and sorting, mutation invalidation, existing detail navigation, preserved original form state, persistence, undo/reset and scope switching.
- Drift protection, removal retaining config/overrides/identity history, and reinstall.

It uses a deterministic test transport, not a live model. It does not install pods, build native binaries, deploy a planner, launch simulators or claim physical-device acceptance. Those are separate checks below. Fixture source is in fixtures/fresh-react-native in the SDK checkout; the CLI steps are replayed by scripts/consumer.

## Native Jest setup

The SDK's native package entry points use built JavaScript. Standard React Native Jest does not need a transform exception for @customitin. Existing host libraries can still require their normal native mocks or ESM transform settings.

If using AsyncStorage and safe-area-context, add a Jest setup file:

```js
/* eslint-env jest */
jest.mock('@react-native-async-storage/async-storage', () =>
  require('@react-native-async-storage/async-storage/jest/async-storage-mock'),
);
jest.mock(
  'react-native-safe-area-context',
  () => require('react-native-safe-area-context/jest/mock').default,
);
```

Merge it into the app's Jest config. For the documented React Navigation example:

```js
module.exports = {
  preset: 'react-native',
  setupFiles: ['./jest.setup.js'],
  transformIgnorePatterns: [
    'node_modules/(?!((jest-)?react-native|@react-native(-community)?|@react-navigation)/)',
  ],
};
```

Preserve existing config and any exceptions needed by the app's other dependencies. Tests can use @testing-library/react-native with react-test-renderer matching the installed React version. Await async actions with act, await the visible result, unmount/cleanup, and clear the app's QueryClient after each test. The template's original smoke test leaves its renderer mounted; when adding async data providers, replace that test with one that waits for content and cleans up so Jest exits cleanly. Do not use forceExit or suppress console warnings to hide pending work.

## Test a proposal without a model key

Natural-language creation requires a backend planner, but validating the mobile integration does not. Use a test-only PlannerTransport (mock personalize/config in Jest or inject it through a development-only host configuration). Never change personalize/root.tsx or generated adapters.

This example creates a list using the first approved source and a compatible renderer. It uses no domain assumptions, filters or fabricated capability IDs:

```ts
import { registrySchema, type PlannerResponse } from '@customitin/core';
import type { PlannerTransport } from '@customitin/react-native';
import capabilities from '../personalize/capabilities.json';

const registry = registrySchema.parse(capabilities);
export const testPlanner: PlannerTransport = {
  async plan(request): Promise<PlannerResponse> {
    const source = registry.sources[0];
    if (!source)
      return { kind: 'unsupported', message: 'Enable a source first.' };
    const renderer = registry.components.find(
      (component) =>
        component.kind === 'item' && component.sourceIds?.includes(source.id),
    );
    return {
      kind: 'proposal',
      proposal: {
        requestId: request.requestId,
        registryRevision: request.registryRevision,
        baseRevision: request.baseRevision,
        summary: 'Show the approved collection.',
        operations: [
          {
            op: 'createView',
            view: {
              id: 'test-list',
              title: 'Test collection',
              sourceId: source.id,
              query: { filters: [], sort: [] },
              presentation: {
                mode: 'list',
                itemRendererId: renderer?.id ?? 'item',
                density: 'comfortable',
              },
            },
          },
          {
            op: 'setSurfaceLayout',
            surfaceId: 'home',
            nodes: [
              {
                id: 'test-list-node',
                componentId: 'collection',
                viewId: 'test-list',
                props: {},
                children: [],
              },
            ],
          },
        ],
      },
    };
  },
};
```

In a test, mock config by spreading jest.requireActual('../personalize/config') and replacing planner with this transport. Keep the helper outside **tests**, or give Jest an explicit testMatch: the standard template treats every file under **tests** as a test suite. Clear storage between unrelated tests; retain it when testing remount persistence.

Open Customize, enter any text, preview, then apply. My space should display the approved collection. To verify filters, adapt the proposal to real allowed field/operators and include a matching record beyond the first host page. To verify a host card or section, select the actual discovered component and provide its required props. Verify that its provider hooks still work. Clicking a card should open the existing detail route after --detail has connected it.

The requestId, baseRevision and registryRevision must echo the current request. Reusing an old proposal is expected to fail. Invalid fields/routes/components must not change the saved profile. This transport is a test fixture, not an AI implementation or fallback for production prompts.

## Consumer checks and native bundles

From the app:

```sh
npx --no-install customitin doctor --typecheck
npx --no-install tsc --noEmit
npx --no-install eslint . --ext .js,.jsx,.ts,.tsx --max-warnings 0
npm test -- --runInBand --watch=false
npx --no-install react-native bundle --platform ios --dev false --entry-file index.js --bundle-output /tmp/customitin-ios.jsbundle --assets-dest /tmp/customitin-ios-assets --max-workers 2
npx --no-install react-native bundle --platform android --dev false --entry-file index.js --bundle-output /tmp/customitin-android.jsbundle --assets-dest /tmp/customitin-android-assets --max-workers 2
```

These are bare React Native commands; Expo apps use their own export/build workflow. A successful bundle is not a native build or a launched application. The packaged SDK resolves its native validation dependencies through CommonJS, so the stock bare template does not need an export-namespace Babel plugin solely for Customitin. If an app imports Zod ESM independently, that separate import can still need its own Babel configuration.

For iOS, follow the template's bundle install / bundle exec pod install steps, then build/run with Xcode or the React Native CLI. With Xcode 27, pinned AsyncStorage 2.2's resource pod may target iOS 13.4, below that toolchain's simulator floor. The fresh-app check used an explicit IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.1 build setting. Align dependency deployment targets with the app's supported minimum in your Podfile/toolchain configuration when needed; do not lower the app's intended support floor or edit Pods by hand. Template/dependency warnings should be reported separately from SDK lint results.

For Android, a Metro bundle still leaves JDK, Android SDK/Gradle, emulator/device, and native acceptance to verify. On both platforms, exercise real storage across process restart, safe areas (including after apply/scroll), VoiceOver/TalkBack, larger text, hidden-screen accessibility, offline behavior, account switching and native navigation. Keep live-provider, authorization, deployment and physical-device claims separate from deterministic local tests.

<!-- Source: docs/ai/cli-reference.md -->

# CLI reference

Run `customitin` from a built/installed CLI package. In this repository use `npm run cli --`. All project operations accept `--cwd /absolute/path/to/app`. Discovery requires a readable package.json; a valid tsconfig improves type resolution. Missing framework dependencies reduce what can be discovered reliably.

## Commands

| Command | Result                                                                                                  |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| inspect | JSON report: framework, entry, versions, symbols, routes/routeDetails, unresolved items, context digest |
| init    | Installation plan, dry-run unless --apply                                                               |
| refresh | Regenerated plan using persistent overrides and binding identity, dry-run unless --apply                |
| watch   | Continuously refresh an installed integration after local edits; dry-run unless --apply; Ctrl+C stops   |
| doctor  | JSON issues, recommendations, coverage and suggested checks; exits nonzero for issues                   |
| remove  | Owned-file removal/root restoration plan, dry-run unless --apply; config/overrides/identity lock remain |
| schema  | JSON Schema for personalize/overrides.json; no host project required                                    |
| guide   | AI documentation index; no host project required                                                        |

## Options

| Flag                      | Meaning                                                                                           |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| --dry-run                 | Preview only; takes precedence over --apply                                                       |
| --apply                   | Write planned changes if there are no ownership conflicts or integration issues                   |
| --context                 | For inspect, include the exact bounded metadata eligible for optional AI analysis                 |
| --complete SELECTOR       | Confirm a discovered complete array/query-options source; repeatable; saved to overrides on apply |
| --component SELECTOR      | Enable a discovered component; repeatable; saved to overrides                                     |
| --screen SELECTOR         | Instrument an existing screen in place; repeatable; saved to overrides                            |
| --route SELECTOR          | Enable a discovered route; repeatable; saved to overrides                                         |
| --detail SOURCE=ROUTE     | Connect row details and enable the route; repeatable; does not assert completeness                |
| --query-client SELECTOR   | Choose an existing exported QueryClient                                                           |
| --navigation-ref SELECTOR | Choose an existing exported React Navigation ref                                                  |
| --typecheck               | For doctor, statically check host/generated TypeScript                                            |
| --ai                      | For init/refresh, use optional installer AI to select complete discovered sources                 |
| --approve-context DIGEST  | Required exact inspect context digest for AI transmission                                         |
| --topic TOPIC             | For guide: index, integration, contracts, maintenance, troubleshooting, testing, cli-reference    |
| --help                    | Print command help                                                                                |

Selectors are printed by inspect. Symbols use `file.ts#exportName` or `file.ts#repository.method`. Expo routes use their file path. React Navigation routes use `file.ts#RootParamList.Screen`. Overrides may also use persisted capability IDs. Quote selectors in shell commands, especially paths containing brackets or parentheses.

## Machine-readable plan

init/refresh print mode, changes, conflicts, unresolved, issues, generated, developerOwnedSetup and contextDigest. generated contains the exact proposed contents of installer-owned files. developerOwnedSetup contains new config/override files or an explicitly requested override merge. Unresolved includes informational discovery gaps; issues identifies actionable integration problems. A dry-run writes none of them. Existing config is never overwritten. init/refresh exit nonzero and write nothing for actionable integration issues or conflicts. Unknown CLI selectors fail before writing.

Screen candidates appear on discovered component symbols as screen.sections, with stable section keys/titles. Ineligible components expose screenIssue. --screen uses the same file#export selector as the component and preserves its stable identity; it does not require enabling --component. Enabled screen selections replace generated My space shell wiring with a provider around the original app. The planner endpoint and persistence remain optional/host-configured as documented in the integration guide.

`watch --apply` runs alongside the host's normal development command. It reuses persisted selections and emits JSON lines containing mode, changes, conflicts, issues and applied. Unsupported edits are reported without replacing output; watch resumes after a corrected save. It does not accept new selections or invoke AI; use init/refresh or overrides for those decisions. Ordinary host code is editable, while generated wrapper imports/props retain structural checks. Watch handles atomic saves and new source files by polling once per second; it does not execute package scripts or modify the host's dev command. Run refresh --apply and doctor --typecheck before a release.

Writes preserve an ownership manifest and roll back known files if a write fails. The manifest supports diagnosing a process interruption. Conflicts prevent the entire apply. remove similarly refuses to proceed if any tracked file has drifted.

## Optional AI context

Set CUSTOMITIN_INSTALLER_API_KEY and CUSTOMITIN_INSTALLER_MODEL on the development machine. Run inspect --context, review it, and pass its exact digest with --ai --approve-context. This key is for optional installer analysis, not the app's runtime planner.

The context contains synthesized field/prop signatures, symbol locations and route descriptors. It does not contain function bodies, comments, domain records or environment-file contents. Secret-like filenames and detected credential literals are excluded. Type literal enum values are metadata and can still contain private vocabulary: review the actual context. The scanner uses bounded file sizes/count/depth; large monorepos should target a single app workspace.

The AI may select existing complete sources only. Selection is validated and retained in bindings.lock.json for later refreshes. AI does not generate executable code or select shell commands. Unsupported patterns remain diagnostics.

Doctor recommendations are advisory: an offline local-device app can pass without login or a planner. Persistent storage is required for saved settings to survive restart. For authenticated data, connect an account-specific scope and verify isolation; the CLI cannot prove authorization from types.
